title: The Bessie Smith playbill that never happened
summary: Carter says he was billed with Bessie Smith but, per Hammond, she did not show up.

bands.name: Benny Carter and the Club Harlem Orchestra

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: So he came. But I'm trying to think -- this Club Harlem orchestra bit -- did you speak to me about Bessie Smith?
I think we talked about that.
You were bringing in Bessie Smith just now?
Oh, yes. That has to do with something you asked me -- you asked me what was that about.

Right. With this playbill which I first saw say in Chris Albertson's book on Bessie, showing that you and she played on the same bill at the -- I can't remember now again, the name of the place -- it was a vaudeville house, I think.
Right. I shouldn't correct you, but it didn't show that we played there; it wasn't a review.
It showed that we were advertised to play there, right?

So you remember, we talked about this before and I couldn't remember ever having seen Bessie Smith in person, much less having appeared on a bill with her, and this same Playbill had also been in somebody else's book -- I'd been familiar with it for a number of years before the Chris Albertson book.

But John Hammond at that time, as I said, was interested in my band, helping me --and he was also interested in Bessie Smith and it might have had something to do with her being billed there with me. About 2 or 3 months ago, John was out in California, with the Columbia Records convention, and we had dinner together. And I asked John about this. "What happened?" I said -- "I don't remember appearing with Bessie Smith." He said, "Oh, you were billed, but she didn't show up."

And as I recall now, in the book, I believe that Chris Albertson said that she had sort of a penchant for not showing up at all times, you know, when she was billed somewhere, and this was probably one of those times when something happened that prevented her from showing up.
